confirmations.description: Establish this stream before calling process. The accounts filter matches a confirmed block owned by a tracked account (including sends and receives), and a state send whose link_as_account is a tracked account. For a send, params.hash equals the process result hash. Deduplicate by hash. When the upstream WebSocket drops the stream closes, as a node closing a WebSocket would; there is no replay and no gap announcement, so reconcile with accounts_frontiers and account_history before applying later events. The filter cannot be changed on a live stream: the node changes one with an update message carrying accounts_add and accounts_del, and SSE carries no client-to-server message. A client that needs to change its tracked set opens a new stream and reconciles afterwards. A client with more accounts than fit in a request line splits them across several streams, or POSTs the same options as a JSON body.
confirmations.title: Confirmation event stream

nano.confirmation.name: nano.confirmation
nano.confirmation.summary: A block from the configured Nano profile has been cemented.
nano.confirmation.title: nano.confirmation

block.description: Native confirmed block content. `subtype` and `link_as_account` live here; the node keeps them inside the block.

election_info.description: Present when the subscription requested include_election_info.

time.description: End of the election, in milliseconds since the epoch.

hash.description: Cemented block hash. For a submitted block, this equals process result.hash and is the idempotency key.

time.description: Event time in milliseconds since the epoch, from the upstream envelope.

accounts.description: Only receive confirmations that mention these accounts. A state send matches on its owning account or its block's link_as_account. Legacy blocks are never delivered once a filter is given.

all_local_accounts.description: Accepted and ignored. It asks for accounts held in the node's own wallet, which is a custodial dev-ledger feature the gateway does not track and does not expose. A non-custodial integrator lists its own accounts in `accounts` instead, which is the equivalent behaviour. This is the one option the gateway does not pass upstream.

confirmation_type.description: Which confirmations to receive, filtered on the event's own confirmation_type. The upstream guide recommends leaving this unset so a notification is less likely to be missed.

include_block.description: Include the block content. Omit the block from the payload when false. Incompatible with an accounts filter, as it is upstream.

include_election_info.description: Add election_info to each confirmation. The gateway always requests it upstream so it is available when asked for.

include_sideband_info.description: Add height and local_timestamp to the block. The gateway always requests it upstream so it is available when asked for.

info.description: Receive-only SSE notifications for a pinned Nano node profile. Subscribe before submitting a block, deduplicate notifications by hash, and reconcile through block_info if confirmation is not observed. Notifications identify account activity; use the native accounts_balances RPC for an event-triggered batch snapshot of balance and receivable state.
info.title: Nano Gateway Events

x-nano-filter-ceiling.why: The node documents no cap. This bound is what an HTTP request line can carry, because nginx and Apache commonly limit one to about 8 KiB. A Nano address is 65 characters, so 110 accounts is 7259 bytes. Use POST, or split the set across several streams, to go beyond it.

receiveConfirmations.description: GET carries the account filter in the request line, which is what EventSource speaks and needs no custom client code. It is bounded by what an intermediary accepts as a request line, commonly about 8 KiB, so roughly a hundred accounts.

receiveConfirmationsWithBody.description: EventSource only issues GET, so a client whose filter outgrows the request line uses fetch and reads the response as a stream. The response is byte-for-byte the same SSE the GET form returns. Requires custom client code.
receiveConfirmationsWithBody.summary: The same stream, with the subscribe options in a JSON body.

x-nano-account-tracking.accounts_filter: Subscribe with the watched accounts before any related process call.

frontier_confirmation.when: Use this flow when the known account frontier, rather than a submitted block hash, is the starting point. Query the current frontier and inspect its confirmation status.

steps: accounts_frontiers with accounts: compare each result against the stored frontier hash.

account_history with head set to the stored hash, reverse true and raw true, for each changed account. head is inclusive, so the first entry is the head block itself: dedupe by hash rather than dropping entry 0. raw is required because the summary form skips change and epoch blocks.
accounts_receivable with source, for incoming blocks that are not yet received.
blocks_info with the new frontier hashes, and read confirmed. If false, escalate with block_confirm.
frontier_delta.when: The canonical refresh. Three batch calls plus one account_history per changed account, whatever the size of the account set.

state_refresh.when: Read balance and receivable totals after a matching confirmation. This cannot detect every change: it returns no hashes, and a representative-change block leaves the balance unchanged. Use the frontier delta sequence below when you need to detect changes rather than totals.

escalation.rate_limited: An operator guard answers HTTP 429 with Retry-After and no JSON-RPC body.

result.started: Always the string 1. It reports that no error occurred, never that the block confirmed. The call also re-fires confirmation notifications for a block that is already confirmed.

sequence: Wait about 5 seconds after a block of interest.
Call block_info with the hash and read result.confirmed.
If it is false, call block_confirm with the hash.
Expect a confirmation notification, then call block_info again.
Escalate any remaining delay in your own systems.
